lines.text: LinkedIn built AI reviewers that check each other, and they cover over 40,000 code changes a week.
AI writes code fast now. So the slow step is humans reading and reviewing it.
lines.title: The new bottleneck

lines.text: A vendor's reviewer was noisy and generic. One model alone made things up and pointed at wrong lines.
lines.title: What failed

lines.text: Several AI agents review the same change on their own, never seeing each other's findings.
lines.title: Step 1: review

lines.text: An orchestrator merges duplicate findings. Overlap between agents means higher confidence.
lines.title: Step 2: merge

lines.text: A different model verifies findings only one agent raised. Weak or cosmetic ones are dropped.
lines.title: Step 3: verify

lines.text: Most reviews are posted before a human even opens the change, so people read fewer, better comments.
lines.title: Takeaways
